Hazard / Risk: Collapse of the soil zone above rockhead; fall of persons and plant into the excavation; fall of material from the edge.
Controls / Response: Battered or supported faces designed as temporary works before excavation starts; edge protection, barriers and signage installed as the excavation deepens; spoil and plant kept back from the edge; access by fixed ladders in protected bays; daily inspection by a competent person after rain.

Hazard / Risk: Flying fragments; noise; hand-arm and whole-body vibration; damage to adjacent structures.
Controls / Response: Hydraulic breaking only, no blasting; exclusion zone around the rig; eye and hearing protection mandatory; vibration exposure monitored; a minimum 10 m separation from the sentry post founding level maintained.
Reference / Owner: IS 3764; IS 5121 for safety in erection — To be verified against the applicable MES SOR/SSR/specification edition.

Hazard / Risk: Water accumulation; oxygen deficiency in a deep sump; entrapment.
Controls / Response: Continuous dewatering with standby; the sump pit at (-)8.100 is treated as a CONFINED SPACE with permit, gas testing, ventilation, a standby person and rescue arrangements.

Hazard / Risk: Cuts and puncture from projecting bars; manual handling injuries; crush injuries during unloading.
Controls / Response: Bar caps on all projecting verticals; mechanical unloading; gloves and safety footwear; bar-bending machines guarded; the reinforcement yard laid out so that bars are not carried over other trades.

Hazard / Risk: Collapse of falsework under the 112 m³ pressure slab pour; falls from the deck at 3.200 m; falling components during striking.
Controls / Response: Falsework designed, checked and inspected before every pour; a striking permit signed only against the IS 456 Table 11 periods; edge protection to the deck; exclusion zone below during striking.

Hazard / Risk: Cement burns and dermatitis; eye injury; pump line whip; entanglement with vibrators; night work fatigue on continuous pours.
Controls / Response: Gloves, eye protection and barrier cream; pump lines restrained and pressure-tested; a briefed pour team with defined rest breaks; lighting designed for the continuous pours.

Category / Activity: Work at height — headhouse, sentry post, scaffolding
Hazard / Risk: Falls from the scaffold and from the slab edges; falling tools and materials.
Controls / Response: Scaffold erected, altered and dismantled only by trained scaffolders and tagged before use; full guard-rail, mid-rail and toe-board; harness where edge protection cannot be provided; toe-boards and debris netting.

Hazard / Risk: Falls from the masonry scaffold at first-storey level; collapse of a freshly built panel; manual handling of bricks and mortar; silica dust from cutting; eye injury from mortar splash and from chasing.
Controls / Response: Independent tied scaffold with a proper working platform, never a trestle on a slab edge; no more than 1 m of lift above adjacent work in a day, and temporary propping of a free-standing panel; mechanical hoisting of bricks above ground level rather than throwing; wet cutting or on-tool extraction and RPE for dust; eye protection for laying, cutting and chasing; the top course wedged only from a proper platform.
Reference / Owner: IS 2212 for the work itself; IS 3696 (Part 1); IS 7969

Hazard / Risk: Load failure during the lift of the blast door leaves, the filter trains, the EMP enclosure and the spiral stair.
Controls / Response: Lift plan for every significant lift; certified crane, operator and tackle; exclusion zone; no lifting over occupied areas; wind limit set for the crane.
Reference / Owner: IS 3696 (Part 1); To be verified against the applicable MES SOR/SSR/specification edition.

Category / Activity: Confined space — sump, escape shafts, ducts
Hazard / Risk: Oxygen deficiency; toxic atmosphere; entrapment in a 1400 dia shaft.
Controls / Response: Permit to work, gas testing before and during entry, forced ventilation, harness and retrieval line, standby person, and a rehearsed rescue plan. The 1400 dia escape shafts are entered only under permit.
Reference / Owner: Permit-to-work system; To be verified against the applicable MES SOR/SSR/specification edition.

Hazard / Risk: Electric shock; arc flash; working live.
Controls / Response: All work dead unless a live-working permit is issued; lock-off and tag; residual current protection on all site supplies; only competent electricians; the generator changeover proved before energisation.

Hazard / Risk: Struck by excavator, tipper or roller; reversing incidents; interaction with pedestrians on a constrained site.
Controls / Response: Segregated pedestrian routes; banksman for all reversing; reversing alarms and cameras; a one-way haul route; speed limit; daily plant inspection.
Reference / Owner: IS 7969; To be verified against the applicable MES SOR/SSR/specification edition.

Hazard / Risk: Solvent vapour in the confined internal envelope; fire; skin and respiratory sensitisation.
Controls / Response: Forced ventilation during application in the closed envelope; no hot work adjacent; appropriate RPE and gloves; material safety data sheets held on site for every product; a fire watch where hot-applied systems are used.
Reference / Owner: Product safety data; To be verified against the applicable MES SOR/SSR/specification edition.

Hazard / Risk: Plant overturning on the berm slope; crushing between plant and the structure; damage to the tanking membrane by plant tracking.
Controls / Response: Compaction plant kept off the membrane until the 100 protection screed is cured; slope gradients controlled; banksman during placement adjacent to the structure.

Hazard / Risk: General site hazards; emergency in a deep excavation or a confined space.
Controls / Response: Site induction for every person; PPE as a minimum standard — helmet, safety footwear, high-visibility clothing, eye protection; first-aid post and trained first-aiders; documented emergency plan with rescue from height and from confined space; emergency contact list and assembly point; weekly safety walk and monthly safety committee.
Reference / Owner: IS 13416 (Parts 1 to 5); CPWD Safety Code; To be verified against the applicable MES SOR/SSR/specification edition.

Hazard / Risk: Groundwater is higher than the ASSUMED (-)2.000. Water is nearly two-thirds of the 15.41 kPa/m lateral gradient, so the walls, the flotation check and the dewatering all move.
Controls / Response: Monsoon monitoring (A1080) is deliberately on the critical path and must close before the excavation support is designed. If the level is higher, the design is referred back before excavation, not after.

Hazard / Risk: Red-bole or vesicular seams found under the mat. A single seam produces the differential-support case that sizes the mat.
Controls / Response: Confirmatory boreholes before excavation; every seam exposed at formation is over-excavated and replaced with M15; formation approval is a hold point with a seam map. Provisional quantity carried for replacement concrete.

Hazard / Risk: Rock excavation quantity exceeds the estimate because rockhead is shallower than the mean assumed.
Controls / Response: The BOQ gives the quantity at both bounds — 944 to 1043 m³ — so the range is priced, not discovered. Roughly one extra day on the excavation.

Hazard / Risk: Blast door FRAMES arrive late. The frames must be welded into the W6 and W7 cages before those walls are poured, so a late frame stops the wall and the whole downstream structure.
Controls / Response: Ordered on day one with a 75-day lead time and 19 days of float; manufacturing progress reported monthly; the frame is a separate delivery from the leaf so it is not delayed by leaf testing. This is the single largest procurement risk on the job.

Hazard / Risk: CBRN filter trains, blast valves or the EMP enclosure arrive late.
Controls / Response: All ordered at mobilisation; each carries over 100 days of float; the installation activities sit after the structure is complete so a slip is absorbed rather than propagated.

Hazard / Risk: Conflict C21 — the CBRN filter duty was stated as 2 x 250 m³/h in master A.3 and as 300 m³/h in nine places on sheet S-06, and 250 fails S-06's own 264 m³/h criterion. RULED AT 300 BY RC1, 10 Sep 2026 (master Part H.14 / K.1 U13): A.3 has been CORRECTED to 2 x 300 m³/h. CLOSED.
Controls / Response: The risk is retired. The enquiry activity stays programmed ahead of order placement, which is good practice regardless, and the owner's own cost estimate independently prices 2 x 300 m³/h.

Hazard / Risk: Conflict C16 — the roof/platform junction, 250 against 500. RULED AT 250 BY RC1, 10 Sep 2026 (master Part H.14): the A.4.7 clause that said 500 has been CORRECTED. It was one clause against four parts of the project and against the geometry - the headhouse occupies Y 200-6000 and the platform is at Y 6000-7500, so they do not touch. CLOSED.
Controls / Response: The risk is retired. The covered entry stairwell roof is 250 throughout, which is what Part B designed, A.7.6 loaded, F.2 registered and every drawing already showed.

Hazard / Risk: No electrical design package exists. The scope is confirmed but no circuit, cable, luminaire, distribution board or earth-electrode schedule does.
Controls / Response: Every electrical quantity is declared 'to be verified from final measurement'. The electrical design must be issued before A11025; the programme allows for it but cannot absorb an indefinite delay. Raised at mobilisation as the largest single information gap.

Hazard / Risk: SENTRY POST BRICK MASONRY (SP-B1) — the lintel design and the wall tie detail did not exist when this risk was raised, and the seismic weight of the frame changes when RC infill becomes brickwork. TWO OF THE THREE ARE NOW CLOSED: revision SP-B2 (10 September 2026, master A.4.8 and Part H.12) designs lintel L1 and the tie detail. THE SEISMIC RE-CHECK, WM-V6, IS STILL OPEN.
Controls / Response: Lintel and tie design requested before A8135; the seismic re-check is referred to the structural discipline. The change reduces the infill line load from 13.000 to about 9.9 kN/m, which points the existing V_b = 73.18 kN in the conservative direction — but that is a direction, not a verification.

Hazard / Risk: The Rev F panels are described as BALLISTIC infill. Brick masonry does not give the same ballistic protection.
Controls / Response: Recorded as a consequence of the instructed change so that the decision is visible. If ballistic performance is required it must be reinstated by another means; this package does not assume it has been.

Hazard / Risk: No site plan or ground model exists. The berm volume, access route, hardstanding, several drainage runs and the soakaway positions cannot be determined.
Controls / Response: All affected items carried as 'to be verified from final measurement'. A site plan is requested at mobilisation; the external works sit at the end of the programme, which buys time but not an unlimited amount.

Hazard / Risk: The 112 m³ continuous pressure slab pour cannot be completed without a cold joint — plant breakdown, supply interruption or weather.
Controls / Response: Standby pump and standby transit mixers arranged; the pour is planned as a single shift with defined fallback joint positions agreed with the designer IN ADVANCE, complete with waterstop and EMP strap details, so that an unplanned stop does not become an unplanned detail.

Hazard / Risk: Reinforcement congestion at 150 spacing both curtains prevents proper compaction, particularly at the haunches, trimmer bands and blast door jambs.
Controls / Response: The 150 spacing is an EMP requirement and must NOT be relaxed on site. Mock-up of the most congested zone before the pour; mix designed for workability at 0.45 w/c; small-diameter vibrators and a rehearsed placing sequence.

Hazard / Risk: Damage to the external tanking membrane during backfilling.
Controls / Response: Protection board or screed applied and inspected before any backfill; a hold point at the vertical tanking specifically because it can never be seen again; compaction plant kept off the membrane until the protection screed has cured.

Hazard / Risk: SENTRY POST masonry quality — plumb, joint filling and the interface with the frame.
Controls / Response: Bricks soaked before laying; gauge boxes for mortar; hold point on line, level, plumb and joint thickness at each storey; the top course wedged only after initial shrinkage so the panel does not attract frame load.

Hazard / Risk: Brick supply — availability of class 10 modular bricks to IS 1077 of consistent size and strength.
Controls / Response: Source approved and tested BEFORE order (A1176 precedes A8130); the whole requirement is only about 6 400 bricks, so a single approved batch covers the job. Changing source mid-job requires retesting.

Hazard / Risk: Cement or reinforcement supply interruption during a continuous pour period.
Controls / Response: Reinforcement ordered at 77.3 t including wastage with mill certificates; cement stocked to cover the largest pour plus a margin; stacking to IS 4082 to prevent deterioration.

Hazard / Risk: Monsoon — Pune, June to September. Deep excavation, tanking and cover placement are all weather sensitive.
Controls / Response: Sequenced so that the deep excavation (Dec–Jan) and the external tanking are out of the monsoon; surface water cut-off drains installed before excavation; productivity allowances inside the affected durations rather than an artificial non-working calendar.

Hazard / Risk: Festival holidays are not in the calendar because their dates move.
Controls / Response: A 10-working-day contingency activity (A14098) sits before handover for exactly this purpose. It is stated, not hidden inside durations.

Hazard / Risk: The 14-day prop period on the pressure slab is questioned on site and props are struck early.
Controls / Response: IS 456 Table 11 is explicit for a slab spanning over 4.5 m; this one spans 5.000 m clear. Striking requires a signed permit. The 19 days are in the baseline and are not available for compression.

Hazard / Risk: Percolation test fails — likely on basalt — and the soak pits cannot work. SK-01 is already 2.3 % short of its own stated requirement (conflict C19, CLOSED by RC1 - SK-01 widened to 2.200 dia, 24.19 m2).
Controls / Response: The percolation test is programmed early (A1085) and is a hold point before the soak pits are built. If it fails, an alternative disposal route is a design decision, not a site one, and the programme flags it early enough to be taken.

Hazard / Risk: EMP shielding effectiveness survey fails to reach 80 dB.
Controls / Response: The rebar cage alone gives 0 dB at 1 GHz — the master says so. The answer is the welded steel Zone 2 room plus disciplined penetration protection and joint straps, all of which are inspected as they are built rather than tested for the first time at the end.

Hazard / Risk: Gas-tightness and overpressure test fails.
Controls / Response: Every penetration through the envelope is recorded and sealed as built; the blast door seals are proved before the envelope test; the test is programmed with rectification time and float ahead of handover.

Hazard / Risk: Damage to the completed sentry post by main-works traffic during the remaining eight months of the programme.
Controls / Response: The sentry post carries 118 days of float and is deliberately started only after the rock breaking finishes, which shortens its exposure. Its surround and apron are built at the end with the external works.

Hazard / Risk: Constrained site access on an operational military installation; restricted working hours or short-notice closures.
Controls / Response: Access control established first; deliveries booked; the programme uses a six-day week which leaves Sunday available for recovery without overtime premium on the critical path.
